### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6c5d5c0038a1c616586cc9a5dc832ff80db3296f` — the merge of head `32a489c698aca499a4e399e7c255a4b55a3934b9` into base `7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6c5d5c0038a1c616586cc9a5dc832ff80db3296f && git checkout 6c5d5c0038a1c616586cc9a5dc832ff80db3296f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 32a489c698aca499a4e399e7c255a4b55a3934b9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 && git merge --no-ff 32a489c698aca499a4e399e7c255a4b55a3934b9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `32a489c698aca499a4e399e7c255a4b55a3934b9`
Reviewer: review-c · read 2026-11-16T02:43Z · L1 ACCEPT read (`review-checklist.md`); no contract face, so no L2 record is owed
Implemented-by: `claude/area-E1b-34040` (area S5) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jRMKz5NhWVrE4E1U5x

- **The fix is the card's.** `GET /meta/doc/NAME?package=X` served whichever package registered last, because the metadata service keeps such a type by name alone. Step 2 now declines the service copy when all of these hold:
  - the read names a package;
  - the exact qualifier admitted no address (`exactAddress === undefined`);
  - the copy is stamped with another installed package that is neither X nor X's customization pair (`serviceCopyOfAnotherPackage`).
  Step 3 then reads X's own package slot (`getPackageScopedItem`), falling back to `getItem` as before.
- **The decline is exact.** A copy with no stamp, `''` or `sys_metadata`, a copy stamped X, a stamp the registry does not know, and an `object` (one owner per name, and `getObject` does not read by package) are all served as before. The bare read is unchanged. The types the exact qualifier already judges were already right, because it replaces the copy after the layers.
- **The dev's named deviation is right.** The step-3 package-slot read is needed because `getItem`'s bare slot comes first. Without it, the fix would have depended on registration order whenever a package-less bare entry exists.
- **`Clause-②: no` is right.** An exact address now answers its own holder (ADR-0150 D3). The read used to answer another package's body at X's address, and that was never a declared capability. `Metadata-protocol: none` and the `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` are right. The changeset names the covered types and the unchanged cells, and both are true of the diff.
- **The pins cover both layers.** At the registry, `package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`. On the composed artifact rig, both transports, in `meta-disabled-holder-artifact-door.test.ts`. The dev report (6905395939) has the touched suites and dependents green under the verify lock.
- **Checks:** all 51 check-runs passed or were skipped, none red; `mergeable_state: clean`.

No must-fix, no should-fix. N1 (nit): if X holds no item of the name, `?package=X` now falls to `getItem`, where it used to answer the other package's body. That is right under D3, and the changeset could say it in one sentence. Not governed: the area lands this PR per `landing-operations.md`.
